theoryMore:
**Details the questions use.** `UserDefaults.standard` is the app's shared instance; the read methods are named after the type they return (`string(forKey:)`, `integer(forKey:)`, `bool(forKey:)`). Values must be a *property list* (plist) type: `String`, `Int`, `Double`, `Bool`, `Date`, `Data`, `URL`, `Array` and `Dictionary` of those. A `struct` of your own is NOT a plist type: encode it to `Data` with `JSONEncoder` before saving. `register(defaults:)` only supplies a fallback value used while the key has never been written; it is not saved to disk and a later `set` overrides it:
UserDefaults.standard.register(defaults: ["fonte": 14])
@AppStorage("tema") var tema = "claro"

With `@AppStorage`, the value after the `=` is the default used when the key does not exist.

**Folders and URLs.** `FileManager.default.urls(for:in:)` takes two arguments: the folder you want (`.documentDirectory`, `.applicationSupportDirectory`, `.cachesDirectory`) and the search domain. `.userDomainMask` means "the user's area", which on iOS is your app's sandbox; it is the value you always use. The result is a list of `URL`s, so take the first item. To build a file's path, use `appendingPathComponent` (the `+` operator does not exist for `URL`):
let docs = FileManager.default.urls(for: .documentDirectory, in: .userDomainMask)[0]
let url = docs.appendingPathComponent("perfil.json")

**Saving and loading a Codable model.** `try JSONEncoder().encode(perfil)` produces a `Data`; `try dados.write(to: url)` writes it to disk; to read, `let lido = try Data(contentsOf: url)` and `try JSONDecoder().decode(Perfil.self, from: lido)`. All of them can throw, hence the `try`. The type must be `Codable`.

**Backup and Bundle.** `Documents` is included in iCloud/iTunes backups (keep only what the user created there); `Caches` and `tmp` can be deleted by the system and are not backed up. `Bundle.main` is read-only and signed: for an editable starter JSON, read the file from the Bundle on first launch, copy it to `Application Support` (`FileManager.default.copyItem(at:to:)`) and work with the copy from then on.

**Choosing the storage.** Small preferences: `UserDefaults`/`@AppStorage`. Thousands of editable records with searching: SwiftData or Core Data (see the next pillars). Secrets: Keychain.

**Fetches with entity names and predicates.** In Core Data the model lives in the `.xcdatamodeld` file, and code refers to entities by their NAME as text. `NSFetchRequest<Pessoa>(entityName: "Pessoa")` creates the fetch; then you fill in `predicate` (filter) and `sortDescriptors` (order):
let req = NSFetchRequest<Pessoa>(entityName: "Pessoa")
req.predicate = NSPredicate(format: "idade >= %d AND nome == %@", 18, "Ana")
req.sortDescriptors = [NSSortDescriptor(key: "nome", ascending: true)]
let pessoas = try container.viewContext.fetch(req)
The `format:` text is a small language: `%d` takes an integer, `%@` takes an object (such as a `String`). `NSSortDescriptor` defines the sort key and direction; `NSPredicate` filters.

**`@FetchRequest` and the environment.** In SwiftUI, `@FetchRequest(sortDescriptors: [NSSortDescriptor(key: "nome", ascending: true)]) var pessoas: FetchedResults<Pessoa>` performs the fetch and updates the View. It reads its context from an Environment value that YOU must inject at the root, usually with `.environment(\.managedObjectContext, container.viewContext)`. `modelContext` belongs to SwiftData and does not work here.

**Objects belong to a context.** An `NSManagedObject` may only be used in the context (and queue) where it was created. To carry a reference to another context, pass the `NSManagedObjectID` (`objeto.objectID`) and reload the object there (`outroContexto.object(with: id)`). Passing the object itself is a classic concurrency mistake.

**Saving.** Changing an object only changes the in-memory scratchpad; without `try contexto.save()` nothing reaches the disk and the changes are lost when the app closes. Use `newBackgroundContext()` for big imports and `automaticallyMergesChangesFromParent = true` on the `viewContext` so it absorbs what the background context saved.

**Migration.** Lightweight migration is the automatic one for simple, inferable changes, such as adding an optional attribute or one with a default value. Complex transformations (merging entities, converting types) require a *mapping model*, which you write by hand.

**A complete Keychain cycle.** The four functions take a query dictionary (`CFDictionary`). To save, combine the class, the account and the value (`kSecValueData` requires `Data`). If the item already exists, `SecItemAdd` does NOT update it: it returns `errSecDuplicateItem`, and then you call `SecItemUpdate` with the item's query and a dictionary holding only what changes:
let base: [String: Any] = [kSecClass as String: kSecClassGenericPassword, kSecAttrAccount as String: "ana"]
var novo = base
novo[kSecValueData as String] = Data(senha.utf8)
var status = SecItemAdd(novo as CFDictionary, nil)
if status == errSecDuplicateItem {
    status = SecItemUpdate(base as CFDictionary, [kSecValueData as String: Data(senha.utf8)] as CFDictionary)
}
To read, add `kSecReturnData: true` and `kSecMatchLimit: kSecMatchLimitOne` and call `SecItemCopyMatching(consulta as CFDictionary, &item)`, where `item` is a `CFTypeRef?`; the result comes back as `Data`. Always compare the `OSStatus` with `errSecSuccess`.

**Protection classes.** `kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlocked...` only allows reading while the device is unlocked; `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlock` allows reading after the first unlock since the device booted, which background tasks need while the screen is locked. The `ThisDeviceOnly` suffix keeps the item out of backups and off other devices.

**Biometrics.** `LAContext` (LocalAuthentication framework) shows Face ID/Touch ID, and it authenticates the PERSON, without storing or encrypting the secret. Before asking, call `canEvaluatePolicy`; if biometrics are not available, offer an alternative such as the device passcode (`.deviceOwnerAuthentication`) instead of locking the user out. Only Face ID requires the `NSFaceIDUsageDescription` key in Info.plist; Touch ID does not.

**Network.** ATS blocks HTTP by default; `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads` turns it off for the whole app and should be avoided (add per-domain exceptions, only if needed). *Certificate pinning* accepts only the expected certificate or public key; it reduces *man-in-the-middle* attacks, but you must plan for certificate renewal.

**The provider in three methods.** `placeholder(in:)` returns the sketch shown while data loads; `getSnapshot(in:completion:)` returns a quick entry for the widget gallery; `getTimeline(in:completion:)` returns the real timeline. Each `TimelineEntry` requires just a `date` property:
struct ClimaEntry: TimelineEntry { let date: Date; let temperatura: Int }
completion(Timeline(entries: entradas, policy: .after(Date().addingTimeInterval(900))))
The `.after(date)` policy asks for a new timeline from that date on; `.atEnd` asks when the entries run out; `.never` never asks, and the system only reloads when the app calls `WidgetCenter`. The system may delay the request (daily budget), so prefer several ready-made future entries. For countdowns, `Text(date, style: .timer)` updates itself without spending reloads.

**Configuration types and sizes.** `StaticConfiguration` has no editable options. For the user to edit parameters (for example, pick a city), use `AppIntentConfiguration` with a `WidgetConfigurationIntent` whose properties carry `@Parameter`. `.supportedFamilies([.systemSmall])` limits the sizes (small is the smallest Home Screen size).

**Updating from the app.** The app and the extension are separate processes, so `UserDefaults.standard` is NOT shared: write to an App Group, `UserDefaults(suiteName: "group.com.empresa.app")`, in both targets, and then call `WidgetCenter.shared.reloadAllTimelines()` (or `reloadTimelines(ofKind: "Clima")` for a single widget).

**Interaction and background.** Widgets do not scroll or accept typing. Only `Button(intent:)` and `Toggle(isOn:intent:)`, tied to an App Intent (see the App Intents pillar), do anything without opening the app. To open a screen of the app, use `.widgetURL(URL(string: "meuapp://tarefa/1"))` or `Link`, and handle the URL in the app with `.onOpenURL`. Since iOS 17 the background must be declared with `.containerBackground(.fill.tertiary, for: .widget)` so the system can adapt or remove it (StandBy).

**Preview and Live Activities.** `#Preview(as: .systemSmall) { MeuWidget() } timeline: { Entrada(...); Entrada(...) }` shows the entries in the canvas. A Live Activity (ActivityKit) has its interface in an `ActivityConfiguration` in the same extension, but it is started and updated by the app with `Activity.request` and `update`.
